blocks.title: Introduction to Matrices
teacherCues: Write a 2×2 matrix on the board, e.g., [[1,2],[3,4]]. Ask: How many rows and columns? (2×2) What is the entry in row 2, column 1? (3)
Explain that matrices are a compact way to represent systems of equations, with rows representing equations and columns representing variables.

discoveryHook.scenario: A matrix is like a spreadsheet of numbers. Instead of writing long equations with x, y, z, you can store just the coefficients in a grid and manipulate the whole system at once—saving time and reducing errors.

explanation: A [[kw:matrix]] is a rectangular array of numbers. The dimension is rows × columns (e.g., 2×3).
The entry in row i, column j is denoted $a_{ij}$. For a square matrix, the diagonal from top-left to bottom-right is the [[kw:main diagonal]].
The [[kw:augmented matrix]] of a linear system includes the coefficients and the constants (separated by a vertical line).
To form it, write each equation in standard form with variables aligned; use 0 for missing variables.

rows.1: [[1, -4, 3 | 5], ...] but we need proper formatting. I'll represent as text: 1 -4 3 | 5; -1 3 -1 | -3; 2 0 -4 | 6. Actually format as a matrix with rows.

examples.title: A – Find dimensions
examples.prompt: What is the dimension of the matrix $\begin{bmatrix} 5 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$?

examples.title: B – Build an augmented matrix
examples.prompt: Write the augmented matrix for the system: $x + 2y - z = 0$, $-x + y + 3z = 5$, $2x + z = -2$.
examples.peerPrompt: Explain to your partner: Where do the constants go? What do you put for the missing y term in the third equation?

examples.title: C – Identify an entry
examples.prompt: In the matrix $\begin{bmatrix} 4 & -1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 7 \end{bmatrix}$, what is the value of $a_{23}$?

confusionCorner.title: Don't forget the zeros
confusionCorner.body: If a variable is missing in an equation, its coefficient is 0. Always include that 0 in the matrix; otherwise columns will be misaligned.

questions.prompt: A matrix with 3 rows and 2 columns has dimension ___ × 2.
In the augmented matrix, the coefficients and constant terms are separated by a ___ line.
hints: It's a line that goes up and down.

questions.prompt: What entry is in row 1, column 2 of $\begin{bmatrix} 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$? (Enter a number)
hints: Second number in the first row.

blocks.title: Elementary Row Operations
teacherCues: Show a matrix and perform an operation: swap rows, multiply a row by 2, add 2 times row 1 to row 3. Ask: What is the notation?
Explain that these operations produce equivalent systems, just like with equations.

discoveryHook.scenario: Think of row operations like editing a spreadsheet: you can swap rows, scale a row up or down, or add one row to another to simplify the numbers. These tools help you untangle the system without changing the solution.

explanation: [[kw:Elementary row operations]] on an augmented matrix preserve the solution set of the corresponding linear system.
1. Swap two rows: $R_a \leftrightarrow R_b$.
2. Multiply a row by a nonzero constant: $cR_a$ ($c \neq 0$).
3. Add a multiple of one row to another: $cR_a + R_b \to R_b$ (replaces row b).
The new matrix is [[kw:row-equivalent]] to the original.

rows.2: Each entry in row1 is halved

formulaCard.title: Row Operations Notation
notes: Write the operation beside the row that changes.

examples.title: B – Add multiple of row
examples.prompt: Perform $-2R_1 + R_3 \to R_3$ on the matrix $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 5 \end{bmatrix}$.
examples.peerPrompt: Explain to your partner: Multiply row1 by -2, then add to row3. Write the new row3.
steps: New matrix: row1, row2 unchanged, row3 becomes [0, -3, 13].

examples.title: C – Multiply a row
steps: Divide each entry in row3 by 2.

confusionCorner.title: Only multiply by nonzero
confusionCorner.body: You can multiply a row by any nonzero constant. Multiplying by zero would make the whole row zero, losing information.

questions.prompt: The row operation that swaps two rows is denoted $R_a \leftrightarrow$ ___.
When multiplying a row by a constant, the constant must be ___ (nonzero/zero).
hints: It must change the row without destroying information.

questions.prompt: After performing $cR_a + R_b \to R_b$, the row that changes is row ___.
hints: The arrow points to the row being replaced.

blocks.title: Gaussian Elimination with Matrices
teacherCues: Take the system from earlier and write its augmented matrix. Perform row operations to get row-echelon form (stair-step pattern with leading 1s).
Show how back-substitution works from the matrix form.

discoveryHook.scenario: By using row operations, you can transform a messy matrix into a neat staircase pattern. Then, just like climbing stairs backward, you solve for the variables from the last row up—no need to rewrite equations every time.

explanation: [[kw:Gaussian elimination]] uses row operations to convert an augmented matrix to [[kw:row-echelon form]]:
1. Any row of all zeros is at the bottom.
2. The first nonzero entry in each row is 1 (leading 1).
3. The leading 1 in a lower row is to the right of the leading 1 in the row above.
Then use [[kw:back-substitution]]: start from the last row (which gives one variable), substitute upward to find the others.

formulaCard.title: Gaussian Elimination Steps
formulaCard.formula:
1. Write augmented matrix.
2. Get leading 1 in upper left (swap/multiply).
3. Eliminate below the leading 1.
4. Move to next column and repeat.
5. Continue until row-echelon form.
6. Back-substitute to find variables.
notes: Always start from top left and work down.
If a row becomes all zeros, move it to the bottom.

examples.title: A – Row-echelon form
examples.prompt: Use row operations to put the augmented matrix of $x - 2y + 3z = 9$, $-x + 3y = -4$, $2x - 5y + 5z = 17$ into row-echelon form.

examples.title: B – Back-substitution from matrix
examples.prompt: Now solve the system from the row-echelon matrix.
examples.peerPrompt: Discuss: What does the third row tell you? Then work upward to find y and x.

examples.title: C – Quick Gaussian Elimination
examples.prompt: Put the system $x + y + z = 6$, $2x - y + z = 3$, $3x + y - z = 2$ into row-echelon form (first few steps).

confusionCorner.title: Don't alter the column order
confusionCorner.body: When performing row operations, only change rows, not columns. Swapping columns would mess up the variable correspondence.

questions.prompt: In row-echelon form, the first nonzero entry in each row is ___.
hints: It's the number after scaling the row.

questions.prompt: From the row-echelon matrix $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & 3 & | & 9 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & | & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & | & 2 \end{bmatrix}$, what is $z$? (Enter a number)
hints: The number in the constants column.

questions.prompt: After finding $z$, you substitute it into the row above to find ___.
hints: It's the variable with the leading 1 in the second row.

blocks.title: Reduced Row-Echelon Form (Gauss-Jordan)
teacherCues: Show a matrix already in row-echelon form. Ask: Can we make the solution even more obvious? Use row operations to get zeros above the leading 1s as well.
Explain that reduced row-echelon form gives the solution directly without back-substitution.

discoveryHook.scenario: If row-echelon form gives you the solution step by step, reduced row-echelon form hands you the answer on a silver platter: the augmented matrix becomes the identity matrix next to the solution numbers. Each row directly reads 'x = ...'.

explanation: [[kw:Reduced row-echelon form]] (RREF) adds one more condition to row-echelon form: each column that contains a leading 1 has zeros in every other position (above and below).
In RREF, the augmented matrix becomes $[I \mid \text{solution}]$, where $I$ is the identity matrix (if the system has a unique solution).
You can read the solution directly: each row gives the value of one variable.

formulaCard.title: Gauss-Jordan Elimination
formulaCard.formula: After reaching row-echelon form, use row operations to create zeros above leading 1s, working from right to left.
notes: Start with the last column containing a leading 1 and eliminate upward.
The final matrix should have the identity part on the left if there is a unique solution.

examples.title: A – From row-echelon to RREF
examples.prompt: Continue from the row-echelon matrix $\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \end{array}\right]$ to get RREF.
steps: Eliminate above the leading 1 in column 3: $-3R_3+R_2 \to R_2$: $\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \end{array}\right]$.

examples.title: B – Why is RREF useful?
examples.prompt: Explain to a partner: Once the matrix is in RREF, why don't we need to do back-substitution?
examples.peerPrompt: Look at the final matrix: what does each row tell you?
steps: Each row has exactly one variable's coefficient as 1 and the rest 0.
So the constant column directly gives the value of that variable.

examples.title: C – Determine if RREF
steps: Check row-echelon conditions: leading 1s, zeros below them. Yes.
Check zeros above leading 1s: column 1 has 0s above? No above, OK. Column 2: leading 1 in row2, column 2: there is a 0 in row1 above it? Row1 col2 is 0, ok. Row3 has no leading 1.

But column 3 has a 2 in row2 above the leading 1? Actually row2 col3 is 2 but there's no leading 1 in column 3. Condition: each column with a leading 1 has zeros in all other positions. Column 2 has leading 1, and row1 col2 is 0, row3 col2 is 0 – good. So it is in RREF.

confusionCorner.title: Not all systems have a unique solution in RREF
confusionCorner.body: If a row becomes all zeros, or if a row of the form [0 0 ... 0 | c] appears, the system may have infinite solutions or no solution. RREF still applies but the left part may not be a full identity matrix.

questions.prompt: In reduced row-echelon form, every column that has a leading 1 has zeros in all ___ positions.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: All other positions in that column must be zero.

questions.prompt: From the RREF matrix $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 & | & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & | & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & | & 7 \end{bmatrix}$, what is $y$? (Enter a number)
The process of going beyond row-echelon to RREF is called ___-Jordan elimination.
hints: The first name of the method.

blocks.title: Blueprint Aid – Solve a System Using Matrices
teacherCues: Pose: Use Gaussian elimination with matrices to solve $x + 2y = 5$, $3x - y = 1$.
Outline the blueprint: Understand (write augmented matrix), Solve (row operations to row-echelon, back-substitute), Conclude (state solution).

discoveryHook.scenario: You are organizing two equations neatly into a matrix. By following a clear blueprint—write the augmented matrix, perform row operations to get a stair-step form, and then back-substitute—you can solve the system efficiently, just like a computer algorithm.

explanation: [[imp:Understand]]: Write the augmented matrix: $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & | & 5 \\ 3 & -1 & | & 1 \end{bmatrix}$.

[[imp:Solve]]: Get leading 1 in row1 already. Eliminate below: $-3R_1 + R_2 \to R_2$: $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & -7 & -14 \end{bmatrix}$. Multiply row2 by $-1/7$: $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$. Now back-substitute: $y = 2$. Plug into row1: $x + 2(2) = 5 \to x = 1$.
[[imp:Conclude]]: Solution: $(1, 2)$.

rows.1: Use row operations to get row-echelon form, then back-substitute.
Write the solution as an ordered pair/triple.

formulaCard.title: Matrix Gaussian Elimination
notes: The goal is a triangular form with leading 1s.

examples.title: A – 2×2 system
examples.prompt: Solve $x + 2y = 5$, $3x - y = 1$ using the matrix method.

examples.title: B – Check with original equations
examples.peerPrompt: Plug $x=1, y=2$ into each original equation. Do they hold?

examples.title: C – Try another system
steps: Swap rows to get leading 1: $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2$: $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$.

confusionCorner.title: Swap if needed
confusionCorner.body: If the top-left entry is 0, swap rows to bring a nonzero entry to that position. Otherwise you can't create a leading 1 easily.

questions.prompt: After writing the augmented matrix, the first step is usually to get a leading 1 in the ___ corner.
In the blueprint's solution, what is the value of $y$? (Enter a number)
The final step after reaching row-echelon form is ___.
hints: Substituting values back into earlier equations.

challengeCorner.prompt: A chemist mixes three solutions. The system is $x + y + z = 10$, $2x - y + z = 5$, $x + 2y - z = 8$. Write the augmented matrix, reduce to row-echelon form, and solve.
hints: Eliminate x from rows 2 and 3, then eliminate y from row3.
